topics.title: Introduction & Basic Concepts of GST Returns
explain: A GST return is a formal statement of business details submitted electronically by taxpayers to tax administrators.
Returns serve as the basis for self-assessment of tax liability and facilitate credit transfer to buyers.
All GST returns must be filed electronically through the GST Common Portal, offline utilities, or GSPs.
Filing returns correctly and on time is essential to enable Input Tax Credit (ITC) flow and avoid legal defaults.

flow.title: GST Return Filing Process
steps: Taxpayer compiles outward and inward transactions
Uploads details on GST portal or offline utility
System auto-populates credit and tax liabilities
Taxpayer pays self-assessed tax liability
Electronically signs and submits return

topics.example: A retail trader collects monthly sales and purchase invoices, calculates net tax online, pays the balance, and submits his GSTR-3B on the GST portal.
remember: GST returns are strictly based on self-assessment.
All GST returns must be filed electronically.
Nil returns are mandatory even when there is zero business activity.
mistakes: Thinking physical paper return filing is permitted under GST law.

quiz.q: What is the primary mode prescribed for filing returns under GST?
o: Physical submission at local tax office
quiz.why: All statements and returns under GST law must be filed electronically through the GST portal or approved modes.

quiz.q: Is a registered person required to file a return if no business transactions took place in a month?
o: No, returns are not required for zero turnover
Yes, filing a Nil return is mandatory
Only an email notification to tax officer is needed
Filing is deferred to the end of financial year
quiz.why: Filing of GST returns is mandatory for every tax period, even if there is no business activity (via Nil return).

topics.title: Details of Outward Supplies - Form GSTR-1 & IFF
explain: Every registered person (except ISD, NRTP, Composition taxpayers, TDS/TCS deductors, and non-resident OIDAR) must file Form GSTR-1.
Monthly filers must submit GSTR-1 on or before the 11th day of the succeeding month.
Quarterly (QRMP) filers submit GSTR-1 by the 13th day of the month following the quarter.
QRMP taxpayers can optionally use the Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) for the first 2 months of a quarter up to ₹50 lakh per month.

flow.title: Outward Supplies Reporting Flow
steps: Record invoice details of outward supplies
QRMP user uploads B2B invoices in IFF (Months 1 & 2)
Upload remaining B2B and B2C invoices in GSTR-1
File GSTR-1 by due date (11th or 13th)

topics.example: A manufacturer under QRMP uploads ₹40 lakh of B2B sales invoices using IFF in July so that his buyers can claim ITC in August without waiting for the quarterly return.
remember: Monthly GSTR-1 due date: 11th of succeeding month.
QRMP GSTR-1 due date: 13th of month following quarter.
IFF cumulative limit: ₹50 lakh per month for first 2 months of quarter.
mistakes: Assuming IFF is mandatory; it is an optional facility for QRMP taxpayers to pass ITC to buyers.

quiz.q: What is the due date for filing monthly Form GSTR-1 for regular taxpayers not under QRMP?
quiz.why: Notification No. 83/2020 CT extended the due date for monthly GSTR-1 to the 11th day of the succeeding month.

quiz.q: What is the maximum cumulative invoice value allowed per month under Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF)?
quiz.why: Taxpayers opting for QRMP scheme can furnish B2B outward supplies using IFF up to a cumulative value of ₹50 lakh in each of the first 2 months.

topics.title: Debarment & Rectification of Outward Supplies (GSTR-1A & Prior Periods)
explain: A taxpayer cannot file GSTR-1/IFF if GSTR-3B for the preceding month/period has not been filed.
Unanswered Rule 88C (liability mismatch), Rule 88D (ITC mismatch) intimations, or unsubmitted bank details under Rule 10A also block GSTR-1.
Form GSTR-1A is an optional facility to amend or add outward supply details of the current tax period after GSTR-1 but before GSTR-3B.
Errors in prior tax periods can be rectified in GSTR-1 of the period when noticed, up to 30th November post-FY or annual return filing date, whichever is earlier.

flow.title: Rectification Timeline for Prior Period Errors
steps: Discover omission/error from prior tax period
Check 30th November following end of FY
Check actual date of filing relevant Annual Return
Determine earlier of the two cut-off dates
Rectify error in GSTR-1 filed before cut-off

topics.example: A company discovers in December 2026 that an October 2025 invoice was wrongly entered. It can rectify this error in December 2026 GSTR-1 provided the annual return was not filed before 30th November 2026.
remember: Filing GSTR-3B of preceding period is compulsory to unlock GSTR-1.
Cut-off for prior period GSTR-1 amendments: earlier of 30th November post-FY or annual return filing date.
mistakes: Believing a separate revised return exists under GST; amendments are made through GSTR-1A (current period) or GSTR-1 of subsequent periods.

quiz.q: What is the maximum time limit for rectifying an error committed in GSTR-1 of a financial year?
o: 31st December of the current financial year
30th September of the next financial year
Earlier of 30th November post-FY or annual return filing date
quiz.why: Section 37(3) specifies the limit as earlier of 30th November following the end of financial year or actual filing date of relevant annual return.

quiz.q: Form GSTR-1A allows a taxpayer to amend GSTR-1 details during which time window?
o: After filing GSTR-1 but before filing GSTR-3B for that period
Before uploading invoices on the GST portal
quiz.why: Proviso to Rule 59(1) permits Form GSTR-1A to amend/add details after furnishing GSTR-1 but prior to filing GSTR-3B for that tax period.

topics.title: Communication of Inward Supplies & ITC Statements - GSTR-2A & GSTR-2B
explain: Form GSTR-2A is a dynamic, system-generated, read-only statement of inward supplies that updates in real time as suppliers upload data.
Form GSTR-2B is a static, auto-generated monthly statement of eligible ITC, available to recipients on the 14th day of the succeeding month.
GSTR-2B serves as the official basis for determining eligible ITC to be claimed in Form GSTR-3B.
Section 38 restricts ITC availability if suppliers are new registrants, tax defaulters, or have liability/ITC mismatches.

flow.title: GSTR-2B Generation Cut-off Cycle
steps: Suppliers submit GSTR-1/IFF by cut-off date
System compiles filed inward supply invoices
GSTR-2B static statement generated on 14th of month
Recipient claims eligible ITC in Form GSTR-3B

topics.example: A trader checks GSTR-2A continuously to see draft uploaded invoices, but relies on GSTR-2B generated on 14th August to claim exact ITC in GSTR-3B for July.
remember: GSTR-2A: Dynamic statement, updated in real time.
GSTR-2B: Static statement, generated once a month on the 14th.
mistakes: Confusing dynamic GSTR-2A with static GSTR-2B when finalizing ITC figures for GSTR-3B filing.

quiz.q: On which date is the static auto-generated statement Form GSTR-2B made available to taxpayers?
quiz.why: Form GSTR-2B is generated and made available on the 14th day of the month succeeding the tax period.

quiz.q: Which statement accurately describes Form GSTR-2A?
o: Static statement generated once a year
Dynamic read-only statement updated on a real-time basis
Editable form used to pay tax liability
Final return filed by non-resident taxpayers
quiz.why: GSTR-2A is a system-generated read-only statement updated incrementally whenever suppliers upload or alter details.

topics.title: Difference in Liability and ITC - Rule 88C and Rule 88D
explain: Rule 88C triggers an intimation if GSTR-1 liability exceeds GSTR-3B liability by more than 20% and ₹25 lakh.
Rule 88D triggers an intimation if ITC claimed in GSTR-3B exceeds ITC available in GSTR-2B by more than 20% and ₹25 lakh.
Taxpayers receiving these intimations must pay the differential amount with interest or furnish an explanation within 7 days.
Failure to respond or pay results in blocking of subsequent GSTR-1/IFF and recovery proceedings under Section 79, 73, 74, or 74A.

flow.title: Rule 88C / 88D Mismatch Handling Flow
steps: System detects mismatch exceeding 20% and ₹25 lakh
Electronic intimation issued via portal and email
Taxpayer given 7 days to pay or explain
If unpaid/unexplained, GSTR-1 blocked & recovery initiated

topics.example: A firm declares ₹50 lakh output tax in GSTR-1 but pays only ₹20 lakh in GSTR-3B. It receives a Rule 88C notice and must pay the ₹30 lakh difference or explain within 7 days to avoid GSTR-1 blocking.
remember: Response deadline for Rule 88C and Rule 88D intimations: 7 days.
Mismatch threshold recommended by Council: > 20% AND > ₹25 lakh.
mistakes: Ignoring Rule 88C or 88D intimations, which automatically bars the taxpayer from filing subsequent GSTR-1/IFF.

quiz.q: What is the response window provided to a taxpayer upon receiving an intimation under Rule 88C or Rule 88D?
quiz.why: Rules 88C and 88D mandate that the taxpayer must either pay the amount or furnish an explanation within 7 days.

quiz.q: Under what condition is an intimation issued under Rule 88C for liability mismatch?
quiz.why: GST Council recommended issuing intimations under Rule 88C where GSTR-1 liability exceeds GSTR-3B liability by over 20% as well as ₹25 lakh.

topics.title: Return for Summary & Payment - Form GSTR-3B
explain: GSTR-3B is a monthly/quarterly summary return containing outward supplies, RCM inward supplies, ITC claimed, and tax paid.
Monthly filers must submit GSTR-3B on or before the 20th day of the succeeding month.
QRMP taxpayers submit quarterly GSTR-3B on or before 22nd or 24th of the month following the quarter based on their State/UT.
Under QRMP, monthly tax payments for the first 2 months are due by the 25th of the succeeding month using Form GST PMT-06 via Fixed Sum (35%) or Self-Assessment method.

flow.title: QRMP Monthly Payment Methods Flow
steps: Select monthly payment method in PMT-06
Fixed Sum: Pay 35% of previous quarter cash tax
Self-Assessment: Pay tax based on actual monthly sales/ITC
Deposit tax by 25th of succeeding month
File quarterly GSTR-3B by 22nd/24th post-quarter

topics.example: A registered firm in Gujarat opting for QRMP pays tax via PMT-06 on 25th May and 25th June, and files quarterly GSTR-3B on 22nd July.
remember: Monthly GSTR-3B due date: 20th of succeeding month.
QRMP GSTR-3B due date: 22nd or 24th post-quarter.
QRMP monthly tax deposit due date: 25th of succeeding month.
mistakes: Expecting invoice-wise details in Form GSTR-3B; GSTR-3B requires only summarized totals.

quiz.q: What is the due date for filing monthly Form GSTR-3B for regular taxpayers?
quiz.why: Monthly Form GSTR-3B must be filed on or before the 20th day of the month succeeding the tax period.

quiz.q: Under the Fixed Sum Method of QRMP scheme, what percentage of cash tax paid in the preceding quarter is auto-generated in PMT-06?
quiz.why: Fixed Sum Method auto-generates a challan equal to 35% of the tax paid in cash in the return for the preceding quarter (if filed quarterly).

topics.title: Return for Composition Suppliers - Form GSTR-4 & Form GST CMP-08
topics.section: Section 39(2) & Proviso to 39(7) read with Rule 62
explain: Composition taxpayers file an annual return in Form GSTR-4 on or before 30th June following the end of the financial year.
Tax payment is made quarterly using statement Form GST CMP-08 on or before the 18th day of the month succeeding each quarter.
Composition taxpayers cannot claim ITC nor collect tax from recipients.
Inward supplies are reported invoice-wise in GSTR-4, while outward supplies are reported as consolidated totals.

flow.title: Composition Compliance Cycle
steps: Pay quarterly tax using CMP-08 by 18th post-quarter
Repeat quarterly payments for all 4 quarters
Inward details auto-populate in Form GSTR-4A
File annual return Form GSTR-4 by 30th June

topics.example: A composition dealer pays tax for Q1 via GST CMP-08 on 18th July 2025 and submits his annual return GSTR-4 for FY 2024-25 by 30th June 2025.
remember: Form GST CMP-08 due date: 18th of month after quarter.
Form GSTR-4 due date: 30th June following the financial year.
mistakes: Assuming composition dealers file GSTR-4 quarterly; tax payment is quarterly via CMP-08, but return GSTR-4 is annual.

quiz.q: What is the due date for submitting quarterly statement Form GST CMP-08 by composition dealers?
quiz.why: Composition suppliers must furnish GST CMP-08 by the 18th day of the month succeeding each quarter.

quiz.q: What is the due date for filing annual return Form GSTR-4 by composition taxpayers?
quiz.why: From FY 2024-25 onwards, Form GSTR-4 must be furnished by 30th June of the succeeding financial year.

topics.title: Returns for Non-Resident Taxable Persons (NRTP) & TDS/TCS Deductors
explain: Non-Resident Taxable Persons (NRTPs) file monthly return Form GSTR-5 within 13 days after calendar month end or 7 days after registration validity expires, whichever is earlier.
NRTPs are not required to file an annual return.
TDS deductors file monthly Form GSTR-7 by the 10th of the succeeding month and issue TDS certificates in Form GSTR-7A within 5 days of tax credit.
E-Commerce Operators collecting TCS file monthly Form GSTR-8 by the 10th of the succeeding month.

flow.title: NRTP Return Due Date Determination
steps: Track end of calendar month (calculate +13 days)
Track expiry date of registration (calculate +7 days)
Compare both cut-off dates
File GSTR-5 on or before the earlier date

topics.example: An NRTP operating a trade stall whose registration expires on 25th March must file GSTR-5 by 1st April (7 days after expiry), as it is earlier than 13th April.
remember: GSTR-5 due date: earlier of 13 days post-month or 7 days post-registration validity.
GSTR-7 & GSTR-8 due date: 10th of succeeding month.
NRTPs are exempt from filing annual returns.
mistakes: Believing NRTPs must file GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, or Annual Return GSTR-9; they file only GSTR-5.

quiz.q: What is the filing deadline for Form GSTR-5 by a Non-Resident Taxable Person?
o: Within 13 days post-month or 7 days post-validity, whichever is earlier
By 31st December of next financial year
quiz.why: GSTR-5 must be furnished within 13 days after calendar month end or within 7 days after the last day of registration validity, whichever is earlier.

quiz.q: By what date must an E-Commerce Operator furnish monthly statement Form GSTR-8 for TCS?
quiz.why: Details in Form GSTR-8 must be furnished on or before the 10th day of the month succeeding the calendar month.

topics.title: Other Returns - First Return, Annual Return, Final Return & UIN Details
explain: First Return (Section 40) declares outward supplies made between becoming liable to registration and grant of registration certificate.
Annual Return (Form GSTR-9) is due by 31st December post-FY; taxpayers with turnover up to ₹2 crore are exempt for FY 2024-25 onwards.
Self-certified reconciliation statement in Form GSTR-9C is mandatory if aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore.
Final Return (Form GSTR-10) must be filed within 3 months of registration cancellation date or order date, whichever is later.

flow.title: Final Return Filing Time Limit Flow
steps: Identify date of registration cancellation
Identify date of cancellation order
Select the later of the two dates
File Form GSTR-10 within 3 months of that date

topics.example: A company surrenders registration on 10th April and receives the cancellation order on 20th April. It must file GSTR-10 within 3 months of 20th April (by 20th July).
remember: Annual Return GSTR-9 due date: 31st December following financial year.
GSTR-9 exemption turnover limit: Up to ₹2 crore.
GSTR-9C threshold limit: Exceeding ₹5 crore aggregate turnover.
Final Return GSTR-10 due date: Within 3 months of cancellation or order date, whichever is later.
mistakes: Confusing Annual Return (GSTR-9) with Final Return (GSTR-10); GSTR-10 is filed only when registration is cancelled.

quiz.q: What is the threshold limit of aggregate turnover above which filing self-certified Form GSTR-9C becomes mandatory?
quiz.why: Section 44 read with Rule 80 requires a self-certified reconciliation statement in Form GSTR-9C if aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore.

quiz.q: Within what time frame must Form GSTR-10 (Final Return) be filed after cancellation of registration?
o: Within 3 months of cancellation date or order date, whichever is later
quiz.why: Section 45 mandates filing Form GSTR-10 within 3 months of the date of cancellation or date of order of cancellation, whichever is later.

topics.title: Default/Delay in Filing Returns & GST Practitioners
explain: A notice to return defaulters under Section 46 gives 15 days to file unfiled returns before best judgment assessment under Section 62.
Delay in filing GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-4, GSTR-7, GSTR-9, or GSTR-10 attracts late fees under Section 47.
Section 48 allows a registered person to authorize an approved Goods and Services Tax Practitioner (GSTP) to prepare and file returns.
The legal responsibility for the accuracy of information filed by a GSTP rests entirely on the registered taxpayer.

flow.title: Defaulter Notice Action Path
steps: Taxpayer defaults on return filing deadline
Section 46 notice issued electronically
Taxpayer given 15 days to file pending return
Failure leads to Section 62 best judgment assessment

topics.example: If a dealer fails to file GSTR-3B, tax authorities issue a Section 46 notice giving 15 days to submit the return; failing this, tax is assessed using best judgment.
remember: Notice to return defaulters response time: 15 days.
GSTP enrolment in one State/UT is valid across all States/UTs.
Taxpayer remains personally liable for return errors made by a GSTP.
mistakes: Thinking hiring a GSTP transfers legal tax compliance liability from the taxpayer to the practitioner.

quiz.q: How many days are given to a taxpayer in a notice issued under Section 46 to furnish pending returns?
quiz.why: A notice under Section 46 read with Rule 68 requires the defaulting registered person to furnish the return within 15 days.

quiz.q: Who holds the ultimate legal responsibility for the correctness of returns filed by a GST Practitioner (GSTP)?
o: The Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN)
quiz.why: As per Section 48, the responsibility for correctness of any particulars furnished in returns continues to rest with the registered person.
